body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the beta-tuned raw full-donor \(\widehat\tau\) or, on \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\), by \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{iid}}\).  Event transport identifies the displayed equality; it is not a definition of the causal target.  Exact finite-sample conditional coverage and the stated vanishing estimator and interval upper rates hold over every nonempty compatible full-design-centered class.  They do not extend to the original class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\): the shared-design witness gives fixed positive minimax-risk and uniformly honest expected-length lower bounds even as the proposed rate tends to zero.  That witness satisfies historical full-design centering but violates event full-design mean stability, proving rate-essentiality of at least the event-side restriction without establishing separate necessity of the historical restriction.  Nonemptiness requires \(B\ge D^2\).  Under design-only geometric beta mixing the restricted-class uniform rates use \(R_{\star,\beta}\); under conditional calendar independence they use the no-log \(R_\star\).  For each fixed restricted class with \(B>D^2\), all four lower channels match; at \(B=D^2\), only treated, smoothing, and the dependence-appropriate spacing channel are universally lower-bounded, with no donor converse.  Historical response laws may be heterogeneous across units subject to boundedness and a common conditional mean.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with one-time densities bounded above and away from zero. Only the stacked historical design process is geometrically beta mixing. This allows logarithmic blocks of repeated local states and entails the uniform spacing scale \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\).
sampling_model.units: At each pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded treated wealth levels. Unit response laws may be heterogeneous across and within cohorts, provided their historical conditional mean is the common \(m_s\); each unit's entire calendar response path is otherwise an unrestricted cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The event occurs at \(t=0\). Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality identify the untreated finite-cohort event mean from the historical path regression.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path lies in an interior positive-probability region and every historical design density is bounded below there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and standardized fourth-moment envelope \(B\); with \(D=Sd\), these conditions can define a nonempty class only when \(B\ge D^2\). Historical training coordinates are exact. The full donor mean is projected once onto the proxy cube and feeds one log-adjusted local-polynomial fit per cohort, selected by normalized Gram shape. The finite-sample conditionally honest interval uses the resulting full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event bounded-cluster Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and one full-sample donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared observable bad sample.

The Holder repeated-measurement prediction rate has sparse order \((nm)^{-2s/(2s+d)}\) and dense order \(n^{-1}\), up to the stated logarithmic qualifications.
A local-polynomial Lepski procedure adapts pointwise to local design mass and local Holder smoothness under observed random design.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression with a generated covariate attached to every training observation through smoothed first-stage errors.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 establish deconvolution rates when latent training coordinates have replicated classical measurement error.
Theorems 7--8 evaluate a rate-optimal local-polynomial regression estimator at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer.
The dependent-data theorem uses large-block--small-block coupling for conditional approximation of synthetic-control prediction error.
Spline and wavelet series estimators attain optimal uniform rates and functional normality under beta mixing and weak moments.
Ordered moduli characterize optimal confidence procedures for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a fixed Gaussian experiment.

body.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path.  Consistency and cohort-average event transport identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces.  The original class nevertheless permits one design-shared event shock to survive arbitrarily many unit replicates: an explicit two-completion witness gives fixed positive minimax-risk and uniformly honest expected-length lower bounds while \(R_{\star,\beta}\to0\).  The witness satisfies historical full-design centering and violates event full-design mean stability, so at least the event-side restriction is rate-essential; it does not prove separate necessity of the historical restriction.  On the full-design-centered class, nonemptiness requires \(B\ge D^2\).  Under design-only geometric beta mixing, matching strict-slack bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and honest expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\), including the unavoidable log-spacing term.  On the named conditionally independent-calendar subclass, the iid-tuned estimator and interval replace that term by \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\), giving the sharp no-log rates \(R_\star\) and \(R_\star^{1/2}\).  Exact finite-sample conditional coverage holds in both restricted regimes.  At \(B=D^2\), the same upper bounds remain valid but no universal donor converse is asserted.

project_justification.gap: Causal financial event-study theory mainly treats linear return contrasts; repeated-measurement regression fixes the query; generated-regressor theory typically moves training coordinates; and synthetic-control inference does not deliver a generated-event-proxy minimax frontier for compounded wealth across both weakly dependent and independent calendar designs.  More basically, conditional cross-unit independence alone does not ensure that unit replication averages an event outcome component measurable with respect to the shared historical design.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture observes historical proxy paths exactly, replicates untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and estimates only the event-date query from an independent donor sample.  It separates unit replication, calendar path coverage, generated-center uncertainty, and shared-design event shocks.  The resulting maximality witness shows why event full-design mean stability is rate-essential, while the restricted positive theory exposes a dependence elbow: design-only geometric beta mixing costs a logarithm in uniform spacing, whereas conditional calendar independence removes it.
project_justification.fill: The project proves event-transport identification, a universal impossibility over the original class, exact weighted-panel algebra on the full-design-centered class, feasible full-donor local-polynomial estimators, and exact finite-sample conditionally honest intervals.  The impossibility uses two admissible causal completions with fixed observed-data overlap and target separation; it proves constant minimax-risk and honest-length lower bounds even when the candidate frontier vanishes.  The maintained beta-mixing restricted class has frontier \(R_{\star,\beta}\); the named independent-calendar full-design-centered subclass has the sharp no-log frontier \(R_\star\) for every \(\lambda>0\).  For fixed \(B>D^2\), all four lower channels match in both restricted regimes.  At \(B=D^2\), the upper bounds persist and the universal converse contains treated, smoothing, and the dependence-appropriate spacing channel only.  No donor splitting, covariance estimator, deconvolution, dense-site assumption, upper local-mass condition, or sequential overlap is used.

body.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and explain why compounded buy-and-hold wealth requires more than linear return matching. Barber and Lyon (1997) and Mitchell and Stafford (2000) likewise motivate attention to dependence and compounding in long-horizon returns. Matching only marginal or mean return paths generally discards within-path dependence needed for compounded wealth; this is motivation, not a theorem or an observational-equivalence claim under the maintained full wealth panel. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates, while Gaiffas (2007) provides a pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), and Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study different generated-coordinate or measurement-error experiments. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest beta-mixing block-coupling template, and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. The banked predecessor proves a no-log proxy-modulus result only in its fixed-query conditional experiment. The new result lifts that phenomenon to the present complete causal panel class, supplies a feasible estimator and honest interval, and proves the independent-calendar frontier for every \(\lambda>0\), alongside the distinct log-spacing frontier under design-only geometric beta mixing.
body.interpretation: For \(T\ge3\), smoothing is algebraically dominated. Under design-only geometric beta mixing, \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\), so the strict-slack donor boundary is \(N\asymp(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta})^{-1/\kappa}\). Under conditional calendar independence, \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\), and the boundary becomes \(N\asymp(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})^{-1/\kappa}\). Thus independence removes exactly the log-spacing penalty and no other channel. The donor exponent remains \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\). At \(B=D^2\), both expressions remain valid upper phase maps, but donor domination is not claimed minimax-sharp because a universal donor lower witness is unavailable.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on event transport.  The vanishing risk and honest-length frontiers require the two explicit full-design centering restrictions; the universal witness proves rate-essentiality of the event-side restriction but does not separately establish necessity of historical full-design centering.  The no-log corollary additionally requires conditional independence of the stacked historical design vectors across calendar indices.  The broader restricted theorem assumes only geometric beta mixing of the design and necessarily pays the uniform log-spacing term.  Nonemptiness requires \(B\ge D^2\), while the donor converse requires fixed strict slack \(B-D^2>0\).  The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the full Holder ball, \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) are fixed, and the results do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp constants.
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of event-transport identification; a universal shared-design minimax-risk and honest-length obstruction on the original class; the exact full-donor coefficient identity; deterministic local-polynomial control; dependence-specific selector bounds; causal-panel lower embeddings; sharp conditional-risk frontiers; and exact finite-sample conditionally honest intervals on the full-design-centered classes.  The obstruction satisfies historical full-design centering and violates event full-design mean stability, establishing rate-essentiality of the event-side restriction only.  Design-only geometric beta mixing yields the unavoidable log-spacing rate; the named conditional independent-calendar subclass yields the no-log rate without importing block lengths.  For fixed \(B>D^2\), four lower channels match both risk and expected length in each restricted regime.  At \(B=D^2\), exact coverage and upper bounds remain, but only treated, smoothing, and the appropriate spacing channels are universally lower-bounded.  No donor splitting, covariance estimation, response-variance lower bound, sequential overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, studentization, temporal-outcome mixing, deconvolution, or moving-Gram term is used.
